newsitem.title: UK: IMRO fines Commercial Union Trustees 95,000 stg.
newsitem.headline: IMRO fines Commercial Union Trustees 95,000 stg.

text.p: Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) on Thursday fined Commercial Union Trustees Ltd (CUTL), a unit of Commercial Union, 95,000 pounds ($155,000) for breaking rules when it advised clients on personal equity plans (PEPs).
In a statement, IMRO said CUTL, through its Taxsave Homemaker Personal Equity Plan, had sold unsuitable PEPs to 94 customers between April 1990 and July 1995.
It said CUTL failed to ensure the personal recommendations made to customers were "suitable" and did not always have "effective procedures to record all information about a customer".
IMRO also said CUTL did not have "adequate compliance arrangements relating to suitability and record keeping".
According to the IMRO, CUTL has already paid 84,000 pounds in compensation for the breaches which took place between April 1989 and July 1995. CUTL will also pay IMRO's costs of 63,630 pounds.
The Taxsave Homemaker PEP has been withdrawn, IMRO said.
Last month, U.K. regulators moved to speed up compensation payments to victims of pension misselling by banks and insurance companies in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
As many as 1.5 million Britons may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions instead of staying in occupational schemes, sources said.
